papers.title: Nature and Scope of Economics: practice set 1
papers.description: 8 original WASSCE-style objective questions on nature and scope of economics, each with a worked solution and the reason behind every wrong option. Written by WASSCE Tutor, not taken from WAEC papers.

questions.stem: Economics as "a science which studies human behaviour as a relationship between ends and scarce means which have alternative uses" was defined by
questions.explanation:
Robbins's scarcity definition (1932) is the one most widely used today.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- Adam Smith: Adam Smith gave the wealth definition.
- Alfred Marshall: Alfred Marshall gave the welfare definition.
- John Maynard Keynes: Keynes is known for macroeconomics, not this definition.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a normative statement?
questions.explanation:
Normative statements say what ought to be; the word 'should' is the clue.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- The price of fuel rose by 10% last year.  
  This can be checked against the facts, so it is positive.
- A rise in price reduces the quantity demanded.  
  This can be tested, so it is positive.
- Sierra Leone held a census in 2015.  
  This is a checkable fact, so it is positive.

options.label: A
options.content: The price of fuel rose by 10% last year.

options.label: B
options.content: A rise in price reduces the quantity demanded.

options.label: C
options.content: Sierra Leone held a census in 2015.

options.label: D
options.content: The government should reduce the price of fuel.

questions.stem: Which of these is studied in microeconomics?
questions.explanation:
Microeconomics studies individual units: one consumer, one firm, one market.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- The level of national income: National income is a macroeconomic total.
- The general rate of inflation: The general price level is a macroeconomic topic.
- The national unemployment rate: Unemployment for the whole economy is macroeconomics.

options.label: D
options.content: How a firm decides how much to produce

questions.stem: Economics is described as a social science because it
questions.explanation:
Like sociology and political science, economics studies people's behaviour in society.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- relies on laboratory experiments: Economists rarely use laboratory experiments.
- deals only with money: Economics deals with choices and resources, not only money.
- produces laws as exact as those of physics: Economic laws are tendencies that hold ceteris paribus.

options.label: C
options.content: produces laws as exact as those of physics

questions.stem: The phrase *ceteris paribus* means
questions.explanation:
Economic laws hold only if other influences do not change at the same time.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- all things change together: It means the opposite: other influences are held constant.
- in the long run: It is not about time.
- by definition: It is a condition, not a definition.

questions.stem: The deductive method of economic reasoning moves from
questions.explanation:
Deduction starts with general principles and reasons logically to specific conclusions.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- particular facts to general laws: That is the inductive method.
- opinions to facts: Reasoning does not turn opinions into facts.
- graphs to tables: This describes presenting data, not reasoning.

questions.stem: Adam Smith's definition of economics emphasised
questions.explanation:
Adam Smith described economics as the science of wealth.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- welfare: Welfare was Alfred Marshall's emphasis.
- scarcity and choice: That was Lionel Robbins's emphasis.
- economic growth and development: This was not the focus of Smith's definition.

questions.stem: Which of these is a macroeconomic variable?
questions.explanation:
Macroeconomics deals with totals and averages for the whole economy.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- the price of a bag of rice: One price in one market is microeconomic.
- the wage of a teacher: One occupation's wage is microeconomic.
- the output of one bakery: One firm's output is microeconomic.

options.label: B
options.content: the price of a bag of rice

papers.title: Basic Concepts of Economics: practice set 1
papers.description: 8 original WASSCE-style objective questions on basic concepts of economics, each with a worked solution and the reason behind every wrong option. Written by WASSCE Tutor, not taken from WAEC papers.

questions.stem: Scarcity in economics means that
questions.explanation:
Scarcity is relative: wants are unlimited while the means to satisfy them are limited.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- goods are rare: Rice is common but still scarce in the economic sense.
- goods are expensive: High prices are a result of scarcity, not its meaning.
- a country has no resources: Every country has resources; they are limited relative to wants.

options.label: C
options.content: resources are limited in relation to human wants

questions.stem: The opportunity cost of a choice is
questions.explanation:
Opportunity (real) cost is the value of the next best alternative forgone.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- the money price paid: That is the money cost.
- all the alternatives given up: Only the next best alternative counts.
- the cost of producing the good: That is the production cost.

options.label: C
options.content: the cost of producing the good

options.label: D
options.content: the next best alternative given up

questions.stem: Which of the following is a free good?
questions.explanation:
A free good is so plentiful that it has no price and no one gives anything up to get it.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- treated pipe-borne water: Resources are used to treat and pipe it, so it is scarce and priced.
- rice: Rice is scarce and has a price.
- electricity: Electricity is produced at a cost and sold.

questions.stem: A community's PPC passes through C (4 bags of rice, 14 of cassava) and D (6 bags of rice, 8 of cassava). What is the opportunity cost of moving from C to D?
questions.explanation:
Cassava falls from 14 to 8, so 6 bags of cassava are given up for 2 more bags of rice.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- 2 bags of cassava: That is the extra rice gained, not the cassava given up.
- 8 bags of cassava: That is the cassava produced at D.
- 14 bags of cassava: That is the cassava produced at C.

questions.stem: A point inside a production possibility curve shows
questions.explanation:
Inside the curve, more of both goods could be produced with the same resources.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- economic growth: Growth is shown by the whole curve shifting outwards.
- an output that cannot be reached: That is a point outside the curve.
- full employment of resources: Full employment is shown by points on the curve.

options.label: B
options.content: an output that cannot be reached

questions.stem: An outward shift of the whole production possibility curve shows
questions.explanation:
More resources or better technology let the economy produce more of both goods.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- rising opportunity cost: Opportunity cost is shown by movement along the curve.
- unemployment: Unemployment is a point inside the curve.
- a movement along the curve: A shift of the curve is not a movement along it.

questions.stem: Fatu has NLe 50. Her wants, in order, are a book, a dress and a bag, each costing NLe 50. She buys the book. Her opportunity cost is
questions.explanation:
The dress is her next best alternative, so it is the opportunity cost of the book.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- the bag: The bag is her third choice, not the next best.
- the dress and the bag: Only the next best alternative counts.
- NLe 50: That is the money cost, not the opportunity cost.

questions.stem: A scale of preference is
questions.explanation:
Ranking wants helps a person satisfy the most pressing ones first.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- a list of the prices of goods: Prices are not a ranking of wants.
- a table of opportunity costs: It ranks wants; opportunity cost follows from it.
- a graph of demand: A demand curve is something else.

options.label: A
options.content: a list of the prices of goods

options.label: C
options.content: a list of wants arranged in order of importance

papers.title: Tools of Economic Analysis: practice set 1
papers.description: 8 original WASSCE-style objective questions on tools of economic analysis, each with a worked solution and the reason behind every wrong option. Written by WASSCE Tutor, not taken from WAEC papers.

questions.stem: A kiosk sells 12, 15, 15, 18 and 20 bags of rice on five days. What is the mean daily sale?
questions.explanation:
$\bar{x} = \dfrac{12 + 15 + 15 + 18 + 20}{5} = \dfrac{80}{5} = 16$ bags.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- 15 bags: That is the mode (and the median), not the mean.
- 80 bags: That is the total; divide by the number of days.
- 20 bags: You divided by 4 instead of 5.

questions.stem: What is the median of 7, 3, 9, 4 and 6?
questions.explanation:
In order: 3, 4, 6, 7, 9. The middle (3rd) value is 6.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- 9: You took the middle of the unsorted list; arrange the values in order first.
- 5.8: That is the mean.
- 3: That is the position of the median (the 3rd value), not its value.

questions.stem: The ages of nine pupils are 15, 16, 16, 16, 17, 17, 18, 19 and 20. What is the modal age?
questions.explanation:
16 occurs three times, more than any other age, so the mode is 16.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- 3 years: That is how often 16 occurs (its frequency), not the mode itself.
- 17 years: That is the median (the 5th value).
- 17.11 years: That is the mean.

questions.stem: A household spends NLe 150 of its NLe 600 monthly budget on rent. What angle represents rent on a pie chart?
questions.explanation:
Angle $= \dfrac{150}{600} \times 360^\circ = 90^\circ$.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- 25 degrees: That is the percentage of the budget, not the angle.
- 150 degrees: That is the amount spent, not the angle.
- 4 degrees: You divided the total by the item.

questions.stem: A cup of rice costs NLe 9, 12, 10, 14 and 11 in five markets. What is the range of prices?
questions.explanation:
Range = highest − lowest = 14 − 9 = NLe 5.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- 11.2 NLe: That is the mean.
- 23 NLe: You added the highest and lowest; the range is their difference.
- 11 NLe: That is the median.

questions.stem: Which is the most suitable way to show how a household's spending is shared between food, rent and transport?
questions.explanation:
A pie chart shows each item's share of a whole.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- a line graph: Line graphs show changes over time.
- a histogram: Histograms show grouped frequency data.
- a scatter diagram: Scatter diagrams show the relationship between two variables.

questions.stem: In a histogram, the bars
questions.explanation:
A histogram shows a frequency distribution of continuous, grouped data.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- are separated by equal gaps: Gaps are used in bar charts, not histograms.
- must all be the same height: Heights show different frequencies.
- show changes over time: Line graphs show changes over time.

options.label: A
options.content: touch each other because the classes are continuous

options.label: C
options.content: must all be the same height

questions.stem: In a survey, 3 households have 2 members, 5 have 3 members and 2 have 4 members. What is the mean household size?
questions.explanation:
$\bar{x} = \dfrac{\sum fx}{\sum f} = \dfrac{6 + 15 + 8}{10} = \dfrac{29}{10} = 2.9$.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- 9.67 members: You divided Σfx by the number of different sizes (3), not by Σf (10).
- 3 members: That is the mode.
- 29 members: That is Σfx; divide by the total frequency.

papers.title: Economic Systems: practice set 1
papers.description: 8 original WASSCE-style objective questions on economic systems, each with a worked solution and the reason behind every wrong option. Written by WASSCE Tutor, not taken from WAEC papers.

questions.stem: In a capitalist economy, most productive resources are owned by
questions.explanation:
Private ownership of the means of production is the basic feature of capitalism.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- the state: State ownership is a feature of socialism.
- the community as a whole: Communal ownership is typical of traditional or socialist systems.
- foreign governments: Ownership by foreign governments is not a feature of capitalism.

questions.stem: Resources are allocated mainly by the price mechanism in
questions.explanation:
In a free market, prices set by demand and supply decide what is produced.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- a socialist economy: Socialism allocates resources by central planning.
- a traditional economy: A traditional economy relies on custom.
- a command economy: A command economy is another name for a planned economy.

questions.stem: A main feature of a socialist economy is
questions.explanation:
In socialism, planners decide what, how and for whom to produce.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- consumer sovereignty: Consumer sovereignty is a feature of capitalism.
- the profit motive: Profit is the main motive in capitalism.
- free enterprise: Free enterprise belongs to capitalism.

questions.stem: The economic system of Sierra Leone is best described as
questions.explanation:
Both the private sector and the government own resources and produce goods and services.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- pure capitalism: The government also owns enterprises and provides services.
- pure socialism: Most farms, shops and transport are privately run.
- a traditional economy only: Traditional features exist, but the economy as a whole is mixed.

questions.stem: In a traditional economy, the basic economic questions are answered mainly by
questions.explanation:
People produce what earlier generations produced, in the same way, mainly for their own use.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- the price mechanism: Prices decide in a market economy.
- central planners: Planners decide in a command economy.
- parliament: Parliament makes laws but does not decide production in a traditional economy.

questions.stem: A disadvantage of capitalism is
questions.explanation:
Those who own property and capital earn far more, so inequality tends to grow.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- limited consumer choice: Limited choice is a disadvantage of socialism.
- absence of the profit motive: Capitalism is driven by the profit motive.
- slow decisions by central planners: Capitalism has no central planners.

options.label: C
options.content: unequal distribution of income and wealth

questions.stem: Consumer sovereignty means that
questions.explanation:
Firms produce what consumers are willing to buy; consumers 'vote' with their money.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- the government decides what is produced: That describes a planned economy.
- consumers own the factories: Ownership is not what consumer sovereignty means.
- firms can charge any price they like: Prices are set by demand and supply.

options.label: A
options.content: the government decides what is produced

options.label: C
options.content: firms can charge any price they like

options.label: D
options.content: consumers' spending decides what is produced

questions.stem: An advantage of socialism is
questions.explanation:
The state can share income and provide services so that differences are smaller.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- a wide variety of consumer goods: Wide choice is an advantage of capitalism.
- efficiency through competition: Competition is a feature of capitalism.
- rapid innovation driven by profit: The profit motive belongs to capitalism.

options.label: A
options.content: a more equal distribution of income

options.label: B
options.content: a wide variety of consumer goods

papers.title: Factors of Production: practice set 1
papers.description: 8 original WASSCE-style objective questions on factors of production, each with a worked solution and the reason behind every wrong option. Written by WASSCE Tutor, not taken from WAEC papers.

questions.stem: The reward for capital as a factor of production is
questions.explanation:
Land earns rent, labour wages, capital interest and the entrepreneur profit.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- rent: Rent is the reward for land.
- wages: Wages are the reward for labour.
- profit: Profit is the reward for the entrepreneur.

questions.stem: Which factor of production bears uninsurable risks?
questions.explanation:
The entrepreneur bears risks such as a fall in demand, and is rewarded with profit.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- the landlord: The landlord receives rent and does not bear the business risk.
- the worker: Workers receive agreed wages.
- the insurance company: Uninsurable risks, by definition, cannot be insured.

questions.stem: A main characteristic of land is that it is
questions.explanation:
The total quantity of land cannot be increased, though it can be improved.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- made by people: Land is a gift of nature.
- geographically mobile: Land cannot be moved from place to place.
- without a reward: Land earns rent.

questions.stem: Which of these is an example of capital?
questions.explanation:
Capital is man-made goods used to produce other goods.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- money saved in a bank: Money buys capital, but money itself is not capital.
- a piece of farmland: Land is a separate factor of production.
- a farmer's labour: Human effort is labour.

options.label: A
options.content: a fishing canoe used to catch fish

questions.stem: Capital formation requires
questions.explanation:
Saving releases resources; investment turns them into capital goods.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- printing more money: Printing money does not create real capital goods.
- higher consumption: More consumption leaves less to save.
- importing more consumer goods: Consumer goods are not capital.

questions.stem: Geographical mobility of labour is
questions.explanation:
Housing costs, family ties and lack of information reduce geographical mobility.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- the ease with which workers change occupation: That is occupational mobility.
- the movement of capital between countries: That concerns capital, not labour.
- the movement of land between owners: Land is a separate factor.

options.label: A
options.content: the ease with which workers change occupation

options.label: B
options.content: the movement of capital between countries

options.label: C
options.content: the ease with which workers move from one place to another

options.label: D
options.content: the movement of land between owners

questions.stem: Labour-intensive methods of production are most suitable where
questions.explanation:
Firms choose the least-cost combination of factors, given their prices.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- wages are very high: High wages favour capital-intensive methods.
- machines are cheap and plentiful: Cheap machines favour capital-intensive methods.
- output is very large and standardised: Large standardised output favours machinery.

options.label: C
options.content: output is very large and standardised

options.label: D
options.content: labour is plentiful and capital is scarce

questions.stem: Which of the following is a function of the entrepreneur?
questions.explanation:
The entrepreneur combines land, labour and capital, makes decisions and bears risk.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- paying the rent of land to the government: This is not a defining function of the entrepreneur.
- supplying only physical labour: That is the role of labour.
- guaranteeing a fixed income to investors: The entrepreneur bears risk; income is not guaranteed.

options.label: A
options.content: organising the other factors of production

options.label: B
options.content: paying the rent of land to the government

options.label: D
options.content: guaranteeing a fixed income to investors

papers.title: Production Theory: practice set 1
papers.description: 8 original WASSCE-style objective questions on production theory, each with a worked solution and the reason behind every wrong option. Written by WASSCE Tutor, not taken from WAEC papers.

questions.stem: Total product rises from 36 units with 3 workers to 44 units with 4 workers. What is the marginal product of the 4th worker?
questions.explanation:
MP = change in TP = 44 − 36 = 8 units.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- 11 units: That is the average product of 4 workers.
- 44 units: That is the total product, not the extra output.
- 80 units: You added the two totals; subtract instead.

questions.stem: Five workers produce a total of 48 units. What is the average product?
questions.explanation:
$AP = \dfrac{TP}{L} = \dfrac{48}{5} = 9.6$ units per worker.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- 240 units per worker: You multiplied instead of dividing.
- 43 units per worker: You subtracted the number of workers.
- 0.1 units per worker: You divided workers by output.

questions.stem: The law of diminishing returns begins to operate when
questions.explanation:
As more variable factors are added to a fixed factor, the extra output from each eventually falls.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- total product starts to fall: TP falls only later, when MP becomes negative.
- average product becomes zero: AP does not become zero in the normal range.
- marginal product becomes negative: That happens after diminishing returns have set in.

questions.stem: When marginal product is zero, total product is
questions.explanation:
TP rises while MP is positive, peaks when MP = 0 and falls when MP is negative.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- zero: TP is at its highest when MP is zero.
- rising: TP rises only while MP is positive.
- at its minimum: TP is at its peak, not its lowest.

questions.stem: Mining iron ore is an example of
questions.explanation:
Primary (extractive) production takes resources from nature.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- secondary production: Secondary production processes raw materials.
- tertiary production: Tertiary production provides services.
- a direct service: Direct services are given to people, such as teaching.

questions.stem: The most important limit to the division of labour is
questions.explanation:
If few goods can be sold, there is no point splitting production into many tasks.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- the climate: Climate is not the main limit.
- the price of raw materials: Raw material prices do not decide how far tasks can be split.
- the number of trade unions: Trade unions are not the main limit.

questions.stem: A tailoring shop with 4 tailors makes 100 school uniforms a week. What is the labour productivity?
questions.explanation:
Productivity $= \dfrac{100}{4} = 25$ uniforms per tailor per week.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- 400 uniforms per tailor: You multiplied instead of dividing.
- 96 uniforms per tailor: You subtracted the number of tailors.
- 0.04 uniforms per tailor: You divided tailors by output.

questions.stem: A teacher giving lessons is engaged in
questions.explanation:
Services given directly to people, such as teaching and nursing, are tertiary production.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- primary production: Primary production extracts natural resources.
- secondary production: Secondary production manufactures goods.
- extractive production: Extractive is another name for primary production.

papers.title: Concepts of Cost and Revenue: practice set 1
papers.description: 8 original WASSCE-style objective questions on concepts of cost and revenue, each with a worked solution and the reason behind every wrong option. Written by WASSCE Tutor, not taken from WAEC papers.

questions.stem: A firm's fixed cost is NLe 100 and its variable cost at 3 units of output is NLe 90. What is its total cost?
questions.explanation:
TC = FC + VC = 100 + 90 = NLe 190.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- 10 NLe: You subtracted; total cost is FC + VC.
- 30 NLe: That is average variable cost.
- 9000 NLe: You multiplied FC by VC.

questions.stem: The total cost of producing 4 units is NLe 220. What is the average total cost?
questions.explanation:
$ATC = \dfrac{TC}{Q} = \dfrac{220}{4} = $ NLe 55.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- 880 NLe: You multiplied instead of dividing.
- 216 NLe: You subtracted the output.
- 30 NLe: That is the marginal cost of the 4th unit (220 − 190).

questions.stem: Total cost is NLe 220 at 4 units and NLe 270 at 5 units. What is the marginal cost of the 5th unit?
questions.explanation:
MC = TC₅ − TC₄ = 270 − 220 = NLe 50.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- 54 NLe: That is the average total cost at 5 units.
- 270 NLe: That is the total cost, not the extra cost.
- 490 NLe: You added the totals.

questions.stem: A firm's fixed cost is NLe 100. What is its average fixed cost when it produces 4 units?
questions.explanation:
$AFC = \dfrac{FC}{Q} = \dfrac{100}{4} = $ NLe 25.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- 400 NLe: You multiplied instead of dividing.
- 96 NLe: You subtracted the output.
- 0.04 NLe: You divided the output by the fixed cost.

questions.stem: A sandal maker sells 3 pairs at NLe 16 each, or 4 pairs at NLe 14 each. What is the marginal revenue of the 4th pair?
questions.explanation:
TR₃ = 3 × 16 = 48; TR₄ = 4 × 14 = 56; MR = 56 − 48 = NLe 8.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- 14 NLe: That is the price of the 4th pair; MR is the change in total revenue.
- 56 NLe: That is total revenue from 4 pairs.
- 2 NLe: That is the fall in price, not the change in revenue.

questions.stem: A firm maximises its profit at the output where
questions.explanation:
Profit rises while MR > MC and falls once MC > MR, so it is greatest where MC = MR.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- total revenue is at its maximum: Highest revenue is not highest profit.
- average cost is at its minimum: Lowest average cost is not necessarily the most profitable output.
- price equals average fixed cost: This has no special meaning for profit.

options.label: A
options.content: total revenue is at its maximum

options.label: B
options.content: average cost is at its minimum

questions.stem: When a firm can sell any quantity at a constant price,
questions.explanation:
Every unit sells for the same price, so P = AR = MR.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- marginal revenue is greater than average revenue: With a constant price, MR equals AR.
- marginal revenue is always zero: Each unit adds its price to revenue.
- average revenue is less than marginal revenue: They are equal at a constant price.

options.label: A
options.content: marginal revenue is greater than average revenue

options.label: C
options.content: average revenue is less than marginal revenue

options.label: D
options.content: price, average revenue and marginal revenue are equal

questions.stem: A firm's total revenue is NLe 300 and its total cost is NLe 270. What is its profit?
questions.explanation:
Profit = TR − TC = 300 − 270 = NLe 30.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- 570 NLe: You added revenue and cost.
- -30 NLe: You subtracted revenue from cost; profit = TR − TC.
- 1.11 NLe: You divided revenue by cost.
